Thomas Adewumi University, Oko-Irese, Kwara State, is set to graduate 153 students at its third convocation ceremony, with nine undergraduates earning First Class honours. The graduating students comprise 111 undergraduates, 24 postgraduate students and 18 vocational certificate holders. The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Francisca Oladipo, disclosed this on Friday during a press briefing ahead of the ceremony scheduled for Thursday, November 26, at the university campus. She said the nine First Class graduates emerged from seven programmes: Computer Science, Microbiology, Accounting, Economics, Mass Communication, Medical Laboratory Science, and Criminology and Security Studies. Oladipo said women accounted for a significant proportion of the graduating class, with 70 per cent of the undergraduate graduands being female. “Seventy per cent of our graduands in the undergraduate category are women, twelve of the thirteen Distinctions in our health sciences programmes were earned by women, and women make up 14 of our 24 postgraduate graduates,” she said. Oladipo said the institution had recorded growth since admitting its first 60 students in 2021, with its undergraduate graduating population increasing from 26 in 2024 to 63 in 2025 and 111 this year. “Our academic programmes have grown from 13 in 2022 to 89, comprising 44 undergraduate and 45 postgraduate programmes, while our faculties have increased from three to 11,” she said. She said the expansion had not affected academic standards, adding that all programmes presented for accreditation had received full accreditation. The vice-chancellor also said all 111 undergraduate graduands had obtained the university’s Diploma in Data Science and foreign language certificates, while collectively earning 916 industry-recognised microcredentials through its x-Certification Model. She explained that the university required undergraduates to obtain the certifications before graduation, describing the initiative as a model designed to equip students with skills relevant to the global labour market. Oladipo highlighted some student achievements, including Team MedPatch, which developed an Internet of Things-enabled smart microneedle patch for the early detection of diseases such as malaria and diabetes. She said the team came second among 102 teams from 24 universities at the 2025 AFRETEC-UNILAG Innovation-in-Health Challenge, winning a N1.5m grant, before reaching the grand finale of the 2026 NBTI NextGen Innovation Challenge in London. She also disclosed that two Physiotherapy students of the university had emerged as president and general secretary of the Nigeria Association of Physiotherapy Students, making the institution the first private university to produce the association’s president. On medical education, Oladipo said the university had secured approval for its MBBS and Radiography programmes and entered into a 50-year partnership with the Kwara State Government to use the General Hospital, Omu-Aran, as its teaching hospital. She added that the university’s national ranking improved from 252nd in January 2022 to 47th in July 2026, according to Webometrics. The convocation lecture will be delivered by the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Suntrail Group Limited, Prince Lekan Adewoye, while Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq is expected to attend as the special guest of honour. The convocation activities, which began on November 20, will climax with the conferment of degrees on November 26. The professional induction of Physiotherapy graduates is scheduled for November 27.
